title: Release engineering: CI, feature flags, phased rollout
summary: You cannot roll back an app on users' phones, so safety comes from feature flags, phased rollout, fast crash detection and a regular release train.
body: **In simple words:** On the web, a bad deploy is fixed in minutes. On iOS, a bad build lives on phones until users update. So you ship in ways that let you turn things off without a new build.

**Release train:** fixed schedule (weekly or every two weeks): branch cut → regression testing → submit → phased release. Features not ready ship hidden behind flags; the train never waits for one feature.

**Feature flags:** remote config that turns features on/off per user %, country, app version. Safe local defaults, kill switches for risky features and third-party SDKs, and a cleanup process - old flags are tech debt.
**Phased release:** App Store rolls out automatic updates over 7 days (1%, 2%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%, 100%); you can pause it. Combine with server-side flag ramp-ups for finer control.
**Health signals:** crash-free users/sessions, hang rate, launch time, key business funnels (sign-up, checkout) compared with the previous version, with automatic alerts and a go/no-go owner.

**CI:** every PR builds, runs unit tests and lint, checks size/launch budgets; remote build cache; parallel test shards; a merge queue keeps main green. Tools: Xcode Cloud, GitHub Actions, Bitrise, fastlane.
**Forced updates:** a minimum-supported-version check from remote config for when an old version must stop (security, API removal).
keyPoints: No rollback on mobile → flags + phased rollout + monitoring.
Release train with fixed cadence; unfinished features ship dark.
Flags with safe defaults, kill switches and expiry.
Watch crash-free rate, hangs, launch time, funnels per version.
Fast, reliable CI with caching and a merge queue.

followups: **A crash spikes at 10% rollout - what do you do?** Pause rollout, kill-switch the feature, hotfix (expedited review if needed), postmortem.
**How do you avoid flag debt?** Owner and expiry date per flag, lint for expired flags, cleanup tickets in the definition of done.
